sources.entry: MagicWall - Set local videos as desktop wallpapers. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/davidullo/magicwall)

summary.one_liner: MagicWall is a native macOS app that plays local video files as animated desktop wallpapers, with a library, per-display assignments, and an optional macOS 26+ lock screen extension.
summary.what_it_does: The app imports MP4/MOV files and folders into a local library, generating posters, categories, favorites, search and rename. Each display can have its own video, and assignments persist across restarts. Playback uses a desktop-level window per screen with gapless looping via AVFoundation. A power policy can pause playback for Low Power Mode, thermal pressure, screen lock, occluded desktop, or battery, and the menu bar offers pause, shuffle, favorites and stop. Favorites can rotate automatically every 1–60 minutes. On macOS 26+, an ExtensionKit wallpaper extension lets the system play the library on the lock screen. The README states that the app has no accounts or telemetry, with only a daily update check and an optional starter-wallpaper download as network requests.
use_cases: set a local video as a desktop wallpaper on mac
play different videos on each monitor
animated wallpaper from my own clips
pause wallpaper video to save battery
animated lock screen background on macOS 26
how_to_run: Download MagicWall-<version>.dmg from the releases page and drag MagicWall into Applications
Core tests: cd Packages/MagicWallCore && swift test
notable: Lock screen wallpaper via a com.apple.wallpaper provider extension on macOS 26+, using hard links so videos are not duplicated on disk
Per-display video assignments restored on launch
Power policy with battery, Low Power Mode, thermal, screen lock and occlusion rules
Developer ID signed and notarized, with EdDSA-signed Sparkle updates
Fully local: no accounts or telemetry
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later; lock screen support needs macOS 26 or later
Lock screen extension uses private APIs (WallpaperExtensionKit), so it is not Mac App Store material
HEVC transcode is listed as todo in project status
